To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for every first-order logic formula with free set quantifiers and every class of graphs with a nice locally tree-decomposition, there exists an O(n)-labeling scheme, where n is the size of the instance.
for every first-order sentence with free set variables, there exists an O(1)-labeling scheme in every class of bounded arborcity.
first-order model-checking and counting can be done efficiently in graphs of bounded expansion and nicely locally tree-decomposeable classes, using short labels.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a general method to construct efficient labelings for first-order model-checking, which can be applied to a large class of graph classes.

every first-order query can be evaluated in O(log(n)) time, and every counting first-order query canbe evaluated in O(log2(n)) time, in every class of nicely locally cwd-de-composable graphs, and in every class of bounded arboritic graphs.

for every first-order query, there exists a constant c such that the query has an O(c log(n))-labeling in every class of bounded expansion, and an O(c)-labeling in every locally tree-decomposible class.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of model-checking first-order formulas is not necessarily related to the complexity of model-counting.
the first-order model-checking problem can be solved in time O(n log(n)) on every class of graphs with an O(log(n))labeling scheme.

first-order model-checking in these classes is not only tractable in theory, but also in practice, as our experimental evaluation shows that our implementation of the model-checker is competitive with state-of-the-art tools.
